info.title: Projammr API
info.description: The REST API behind Projammr: projects, collections, tracks, sessions, their audio, comments and notes. The web client and the share page both use it.

host.description: The hostname your instance is served from

get.summary: Whether the deployment can serve requests
Public preview of an invite, keyed by its token
get.description: Public preview of an invite, keyed by its token. Read by the acceptance page before sign-in.

get.summary: Public facts about this instance
get.description: Public facts about this instance: whether it takes registrations, whether it has an account yet, and what it is running.

get.summary: Search a project
get.description: Search a project. Matches tracks, collections, sessions and assets, plus comments (surfaced as their parent entity). Ranked by trigram similarity with title/recency boosts.

get.summary: Session-save activity in a project, by day
get.description: Session-save activity in a project, by day. Bucketed by local calendar day in the caller's IANA time zone. `from`/`to` are epoch milliseconds. `trackId`, `collectionId`, `labelId` and `daw` each narrow which sessions are counted, and combine.

get.summary: A project's saves, newest first
get.description: A project's saves, newest first. Each carries the previous save's metadata so a client can word the change without a second round trip. `day` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, read in `tz`) narrows to one local calendar day; without it, the answer is simply the most recent saves. `trackId`, `collectionId`, `labelId` and `daw` narrow which sessions are counted, matching the heatmap.

get.summary: Every DAW the project's sessions are tagged with
get.description: Every DAW the project's sessions are tagged with: dit's DAW module id and, where known, its display name. Feeds the sessions table's DAW filter and the manual session form's suggestions.

get.summary: List the sessions a dit set on disk can be bound to
get.description: List the sessions a dit set on disk can be bound to. These are the project's Ableton sessions that no dit repo holds, each with its track, the path and machine it was last scanned at, every fingerprint it has recorded and its newest save's time. The dit backfill matches the sets it finds against these before it binds one to a session.

get.summary: Every artist credited on the project's tracks
get.description: Every artist credited on the project's tracks. Archived tracks count too, and the most credited come first. Feeds a track's artist picker.

get.summary: What landed in the last day and what has gone quiet
get.description: What landed in the last day and what has gone quiet. Renders linked and saves made in the last 24 hours, newest first, and the live tracks untouched for 30 days with their total. Feeds the project home page.

get.summary: Every device and plugin a project's sessions use
get.description: Every device and plugin a project's sessions use. Named by a session's structure, most widely used first. A DAW's own built-in devices are counted alongside third-party plugins.

get.summary: The sessions in a project that use one device
get.description: The sessions in a project that use one device. Every session whose structure names it, most recently saved first, with the tracks that carry it. A device no session carries answers an empty list rather than 404.

get.summary: Every sample path a project's sessions reference
get.description: Every sample path a project's sessions reference. Grouped by path, most widely shared first, with the ids of the sessions that reference each and whether any of them reports the file missing.

get.summary: The sessions in a project that reference one sample path
get.description: The sessions in a project that reference one sample path. Most recently saved first, with each session's status for the path. A path no session carries answers an empty list rather than 404.

get.summary: Recent activity in a project, newest first
get.description: Recent activity in a project, newest first. Pass `entityType` + `entityId` to scope it to one entity.

get.summary: How much storage a project is using
get.description: How much storage a project is using. Also how much of that is the objects its repos hold, and the cap it is measured against, where the instance sets one.

get.summary: Get statuses in a project
Get the label vocabulary for a project

post.summary: Create a label in a project
post.description: Create a label in a project. A name the project already has is a 409.

post.summary: Queue audio analysis for a project
post.description: Queue audio analysis for a project. Duration, waveform, loudness and spectrum analysis for every one of the project's audio files whose analysis is outstanding. Responds with the job id as soon as the work is queued; poll GET /jobs/:id for its progress.

get.summary: The project's background jobs, newest first
get.description: The project's background jobs, newest first. `status` narrows to a comma-separated list of statuses. `recentMs` keeps done and cancelled jobs only if they finished within that many milliseconds; failed jobs stay until cleared.

get.summary: A server-sent event stream of the project's jobs
get.description: A server-sent event stream of the project's jobs. It opens with a `snapshot` event whose data is the jobs a watcher shows: queued, running and failed jobs, and done or cancelled jobs that finished in the last 10 s. Every change to one of the project's jobs follows as a `job` event carrying the row, and a `ping` event arrives every 5 s.

delete.description: Delete the project's failed jobs. Queued, running and finished jobs are left alone.

patch.summary: Rename and/or recolour a label in a project

delete.summary: Delete a label from a project
delete.description: Delete a label from a project. Its links to entities are removed too.

get.summary: Get a project's priority scale, bottom level first
get.description: Get a project's priority scale, bottom level first. Each level carries how many tracks, collections and sessions hold it.

post.summary: Add a priority level at the top of a project's scale
post.description: Add a priority level at the top of a project's scale. A name the scale already has is a 409.

put.description: Reorder a project's priority scale. `ids` names every level of the project exactly once, bottom level first.

patch.description: Update a priority level. Rename or recolour it, or make it the project's default: `isDefault: true` moves the flag off the old default. A name the scale already has is a 409.

delete.description: Delete a priority level. Its tracks, collections and sessions move to the level `replaceWith` names, in the same transaction. The default level cannot be deleted, and the replacement must be another level of the same project; either is a 400.

get.summary: Get a project's relation types in list order
get.description: Get a project's relation types in list order. Each type carries how many track relations use it (`inUse`).

post.summary: Add a relation type at the end of a project's list
post.description: Add a relation type at the end of a project's list. A name the list already has is a 409.

put.description: Reorder a project's relation types. `ids` names every type of the project exactly once, first type first.

patch.description: Rename a relation type. A name another type of the list has is a 409.

delete.summary: Delete a relation type no track relation uses
delete.description: Delete a relation type no track relation uses. While any does, the delete is a 409 with code `relation_type_in_use` and how many in `details.inUse`.

get.summary: Get sessions in a project
List a project's members with their user details

patch.description: Change a member's role. Requires admin, and a role no higher than the caller's own; owner is granted only by transfer.

delete.summary: Remove a member from a project
delete.description: Remove a member from a project. Requires admin, and the member must not outrank the caller.

post.summary: Leave a project
post.description: Leave a project. Any member may leave their own membership; the last owner must hand ownership on first.

post.summary: Transfer project ownership to another member
post.description: Transfer project ownership to another member. Requires owner; the caller becomes admin and the target becomes owner.

get.summary: List a project's pending invites
get.description: List a project's pending invites. Requires admin.

post.summary: Invite someone to a project by email
post.description: Invite someone to a project by email. Requires the role the project lets invite (admin unless it says otherwise; 403 `forbidden` below it), and a role no higher than the caller's own. An omitted role is the project's default invite role.

get.summary: List a project's saved table views
get.description: List a project's saved table views. The caller's own and every shared one, optionally filtered to one kind.

post.summary: Save a table view
post.description: Save a table view. Creates a private view owned by the caller, or overwrites the caller's own view with the same name and kind.

patch.description: Update a saved table view. Requires its owner, or admin; only the owner may change `shared`.

delete.description: Delete a saved table view. Requires its owner, or admin.

get.summary: List a project's custom fields
get.description: List a project's custom fields: `kind`'s in their order, or every kind's when it is absent. Each carries `valueCount`, how many entities hold a value, and a select also `optionCounts`, that count per option id (an option nobody holds is absent).

valueCount.description: How many entities hold a value; what deleting it loses

optionCounts.description: A select field's entities per option id, what removing an option leaves showing its id. An option no entity holds is absent, so read it as 0. Absent on every other type.

post.summary: Create a custom field after the kind's last one
post.description: Create a custom field after the kind's last one. Its type is fixed from here on. Only a select takes `options`; an option without an `id` is given one. A name the kind already has is a 409.

valueCount.description: How many entities hold a value; what deleting it loses

optionCounts.description: A select field's entities per option id, what removing an option leaves showing its id. An option no entity holds is absent, so read it as 0. Absent on every other type.

put.description: Order one kind's fields. `ids` lists every field of that kind once; a missing or doubled field is a 400, a field of another project a 404.

valueCount.description: How many entities hold a value; what deleting it loses

optionCounts.description: A select field's entities per option id, what removing an option leaves showing its id. An option no entity holds is absent, so read it as 0. Absent on every other type.

ids.description: Every field of one kind, in the order they should show

patch.summary: Rename a field or edit a select's options
patch.description: Rename a field or edit a select's options. `options` is the full list, an existing option keeping its `id` and a new one having none. The type cannot change. Values holding a removed option keep its id.

valueCount.description: How many entities hold a value; what deleting it loses

optionCounts.description: A select field's entities per option id, what removing an option leaves showing its id. An option no entity holds is absent, so read it as 0. Absent on every other type.

delete.summary: Delete a custom field and every value it holds
delete.description: Delete a custom field and every value it holds. Saved views naming its `cf_<id>` keep the parameter, which lists ignore from then on.

post.summary: Create a project

get.summary: Get a project

post.summary: Attach an asset to a project

patch.summary: Apply one patch to many collections
patch.description: Apply one patch to many collections. Select rows by `ids`, or by `all: true` plus the same filters the paginated list takes. `projectId` scopes the write.

fields.description: Custom field values to write, keyed `cf_<fieldId>` and typed by the field (a select takes an option id or its exact label). `null` clears a value. A key naming no field of the entity's project, or a value that does not fit its field, is a 400 naming the field.

delete.description: Delete many collections. Select rows by `ids`, or by `all: true` plus the same filters the paginated list takes. Assets stay: they belong to the project, not the row.

post.summary: Move many collections into another project
post.description: Move many collections into another project. Select rows by `ids`, or by `all: true` plus the same filters the paginated list takes. The caller must be an editor in both projects. Custom values the target has no field for are listed in `droppedFields`. A priority level the target's scale has no level of that name for becomes the target's default, listed in `priorityFallbacks`.

count.description: How many values the move drops

post.summary: Preview a bulk move of collections
post.description: Preview a bulk move of collections. Answers the custom values moving them into another project would drop, without moving anything. Takes the body `POST /bulk/move` takes and runs its checks.

count.description: How many values the move drops

droppedFields.description: Per custom field, the values the move would drop: the target project has no field of the same kind, name and type, or (a select) no option of the same label. Empty when nothing is lost.

patch.summary: Add or remove labels across many collections
patch.description: Add or remove labels across many collections. Select rows by `ids`, or by `all: true` plus the same filters the paginated list takes. Every other label a row carries is left alone.

get.summary: Get a collection's full status
get.description: Get a collection's full status. Includes the real status, based on its tracks' statuses.

get.summary: Get a collection's track summaries
get.description: Get a collection's track summaries. Each is an id, title, track number and artwork — the shape the sidebar reads.

get.summary: Get tracks in a collection

post.summary: Add track to a collection

patch.summary: Update a single track's number in a collection
patch.description: Update a single track's number in a collection. Swaps on conflict.

post.summary: Add many tracks to a collection at once

get.summary: One audio per track in a collection
get.description: One audio per track in a collection. In track-number order; `version` `primary` (the default) picks each track's primary, else its highest-numbered version, and `latest` picks the highest-numbered. Tracks without audio are omitted.

post.summary: Move a collection into another project
post.description: Move a collection into another project. The tracks no other collection in the source project holds move with it. A shared track stays and is dropped from the collection. Custom values, the moving tracks' included, carry onto the target's field of the same name and type; `droppedFields` names the rest. A priority level the target's scale has no level of that name for becomes the target's default, listed in `priorityFallbacks`. The caller must be an editor in both projects.

count.description: How many values the move drops

Custom field values to write, keyed `cf_<fieldId>` and typed by the field (a select takes an option id or its exact label). `null` clears a value. A key naming no field of the entity's project, or a value that does not fit its field, is a 400 naming the field.

post.summary: Archive many tracks
post.description: Archive many tracks. Select rows by `ids`, or by `all: true` plus the same filters the paginated list takes. Rows already archived are left alone and left out of the answer.

ids.description: The rows the call changed; rows already in the state are left out

sessionCount.description: How many sessions belong to the rows that changed

post.summary: Unarchive many tracks
post.description: Unarchive many tracks. Select rows by `ids`, or by `all: true` plus the same filters the paginated list takes. Rows already live are left alone and left out of the answer.

sessionCount.description: How many sessions belong to the rows that changed

patch.summary: Add or remove labels across many tracks
patch.description: Add or remove labels across many tracks. Select rows by `ids`, or by `all: true` plus the same filters the paginated list takes. Every other label a row carries is left alone.

get.summary: List a track's audio versions, ordered by version

post.summary: Link assets to a track as audio versions
post.description: Link assets to a track as audio versions. Idempotent; resequences versions and optionally sets the primary. Asset ids that are not audio files are ignored, so `audios` is what is actually linked. `primaryAssetId`, when given, must be one of `assetIds`. `analysisJobIds` carries the ids of the `audio_analysis` jobs queued for the newly linked rows, so a caller can follow them without a second read.

get.summary: List a track's sessions, main first then most recent
The audio that could become versions of a track
get.description: The audio that could become versions of a track. Every audio asset that could be a version of this track — its attachments and its sessions' attachments — each carrying its existing track-audio link or null.

post.summary: Relate this track to another as a derivative
post.description: Relate this track to another as a derivative: the path track is the 'from' (derivative), the body's toTrackId is the 'to' (source). `relationTypeId` is one of the project's relation types; another project's type is a 400.

delete.summary: Remove a relation touching this track, by relation id

post.summary: Move a track into another project
post.description: Move a track into another project. Its sessions, audios and the assets nothing else in the source project references go with it; what it shared stays behind, unlinked. Custom values carry onto the target's field of the same name and type; `droppedFields` names the rest. A priority level the target's scale has no level of that name for becomes the target's default, listed in `priorityFallbacks`. The caller must be an editor in both projects.

A session has no custom fields, so `droppedFields` is empty. A priority level the target's scale has no level of that name for becomes the target's default, listed in `priorityFallbacks`. get.summary: Get a page of a project's collections
get.description: Get a page of a project's collections. Filtered, sorted and paginated. Sort keys: id, title, priority, upc, releaseDate, status, createdAt, updatedAt.

fields.description: Custom field values keyed `cf_<fieldId>`: text, url, date (YYYY-MM-DD) and select (the option id) as strings, number as a number, checkbox as a boolean. A field with no value is absent.

get.summary: List a project's collection summaries
get.description: List a project's collection summaries. Every collection in the project, as the sidebar and pickers read it.

get.summary: Get a page of a project's tracks
get.description: Get a page of a project's tracks. Filtered, sorted and paginated. Sort keys: id, title, priority, bpm, key, isrc, iswc, explicit, tracks, status, lufs, lastSaveAt, saveCount, createdAt, updatedAt, trackNumber.

fields.description: Custom field values keyed `cf_<fieldId>`: text, url, date (YYYY-MM-DD) and select (the option id) as strings, number as a number, checkbox as a boolean. A field with no value is absent.

get.summary: List a project's session summaries
get.description: List a project's session summaries. Every session in the project, as the sidebar and pickers read it.

post.summary: Create a repo in a project
post.description: Create a repo in a project. A project holds one repo per name: naming an existing repo returns it.

200.description: The repo of that name already existed

get.summary: List a project's repos
get.description: List a project's repos. Each carries its adopted sets, with the session that holds each.

post.summary: Total the storage a folder's objects would add
post.description: Total the storage a folder's objects would add. This answers before any repo exists. `bytes` is the sizes of those objects, counted once each, that no repo of a project the caller is a member of holds; `held` is how many such objects add nothing; `remainingBytes` is the room the project and the caller have left, null when neither has a cap. Nothing is linked or stored. At most 10,000 objects a request.

get.summary: List the track's repos
get.description: List the track's repos. A repo qualifies when it holds a set whose session belongs to the track. Each carries all its sets, not only a session on the track.

get.summary: List the collection's repos
get.description: List the collection's repos. A repo qualifies when it holds a set whose session belongs to the collection. Each carries all its sets, not only a session on one of the collection's tracks.

get.summary: A session's branches, each with the hash of its head commit
A session's commits, newest first
get.description: A session's commits, newest first. Each carries the saves it covers, its author's name and its sample counts. `branch` keeps one branch's commits; `limit` takes up to 500.

get.summary: Diff two states of a session
get.description: Diff two states of a session. What changed between them, across branches: each of `from` and `to` is `save:<id>` or `commit:<id>` (a commit stands for the save it names). The answer is the diff the web draws, with `from` and `to` as save ids. A reference outside the session is a 404; a save with no recorded metadata a 409.

get.summary: Machines online on the session
get.description: Machines online on the session. The caller's machines with a beat within 90 s, each with whether it has the session open and whether it tracks the session's repo. Those opening the session come first, then those tracking its repo, then the most recently seen.

post.summary: Accept a render of a session
post.description: Accept a render of a session: attach the audio file, link it as a version of the session's track, and record the save it was bounced from. The session needs a track.

patch.summary: Make this track audio the track's primary version and pin it

delete.summary: Unlink a track audio and resequence the track's versions

post.summary: Queue this version's analysis now
post.description: Queue this version's analysis now. Duration, waveform, loudness, spectrum, tempo and key, whether or not the project analyses automatically; a version already current finishes at once. Responds with the job id as soon as it is queued (the one already queued, if there is one); poll GET /jobs/:id for its progress.

get.summary: One of a track audio's lazily-served measurements, by name
get.description: One of a track audio's lazily-served measurements, by name; 404 while the analysis behind it is still outstanding, which is what queues it

get.summary: Compare two versions of a track
get.description: Compare two versions of a track. This version against another version of the same track, per second of this one: the stored row when there is one, otherwise computed from both versions' stored features; 404 when either has not been analysed or the two belong to different tracks

delete.description: Revoke a pending invite. Requires project admin.

post.summary: Accept an invite as the signed-in user
post.description: Accept an invite as the signed-in user. The token is the capability, and the signed-in account's email must match the address the invite names (case-insensitively), or the answer is a 403 with code `invite_email_mismatch`. An invite that is expired or already accepted answers 410 or 409 first.

200.description: Invite accepted; the caller is now a project member

get.summary: Get a status by id

patch.description: Update a status. Global statuses cannot be changed.

delete.description: Delete a status. Global statuses cannot be deleted.

A key the scope does not accept is a 400; one the caller's role may not write, a 403, as is clearing a row locked at this scope by a caller who may not lock there (clearing lifts the lock); a value for one the instance locks, a 409 `setting_locked` with the scope and the lock in `details`, and nothing is written (clearing it is allowed: the row is inert under the lock). Answers with the hub's view of the keys written.

A key declared unlockable, or one the scope does not accept, is a 400; a scope that cannot lock (a user's) is a 404. Answers with the hub's view of the keys named.

get.description: A commit's own record: its hash and its parent's, the hash of the save it names, its message, kind and time, the branch it is on, and the set and session it belongs to. `ditSetId` is the set's identity in dit, null when the session has none.

get.summary: Download a commit's set
get.description: Download a commit's set. It is rebuilt from the commit's stored objects as a gzipped Ableton set named after the commit's session. A save whose content is not stored answers 409.

get.summary: Download a commit as a zip
get.description: Download a commit as a zip. It is in the project folder's layout: the set at its file name, every sample the hub holds at its path under `Samples/`, and `MANIFEST.txt` last, one `<state>\t<path>` line per reference (`included`, `not pushed` or `outside the project folder`). The zip streams: a sample is checked before its entry starts and listed `not pushed` when a chunk is missing, and a chunk that vanishes mid-entry ends the response as a failed download. 409 when the commit's content is not stored.

get.summary: Download one held sample
get.description: Download one held sample. It is found by the object id a save's reference carries and served under the reference's file name. A hash the repo does not hold as a sample answers 404.

get.summary: Download a save's set
get.description: Download a save's set. It is rebuilt from the save's stored objects as a gzipped Ableton set named after the save's session. A save whose content is not stored (never pushed, or pruned) answers 409.

patch.description: Change a repo's push-samples switch. Editors only. While the instance pushes samples from every repository the switch is locked on and turning it off is refused with 409. Answers the repo.

post.summary: Adopt a set into a repo
post.description: Adopt a set into a repo. Links the named session of the project, or creates one named after the file on the named track, and logs its creation unless `quiet` is true. A set already adopted answers with its session.

200.description: The set is held by an existing session

201.description: A session was created for the set

get.summary: Download a repository as a zip
get.description: Download a repository as a zip. It is in the project folder's layout: every set at the tip of its `main` branch, every sample the hub holds at its path under `Samples/`, and `MANIFEST.txt` last. A set is rebuilt when its turn comes, one in memory at a time, so a set that cannot be rebuilt ends the response as a failed download. 409 when no set has a `main` commit yet or a tip's content is not stored.

post.summary: Record the saves dit made on a branch of a set
post.description: Record the saves dit made on a branch of a set. A save already recorded has its metadata refreshed; a save recorded at the same time without content is given the content. The first mention of a branch creates it. The `X-Machine-Id` header names the pushing machine, which a save naming that machine's name takes as its own: a 409 `machine_not_registered` when no machine holds the id, a 401 when it was removed.

post.summary: Record the spans of time a set was open
post.description: Record the spans of time a set was open. A span pushed again keeps its start and takes the later of its ends, so a re-push counts once. The `X-Machine-Id` header names the pushing machine, as for saves.

post.summary: Record commits on a branch of a set, in order
post.description: Record commits on a branch of a set, in order. Each continues the branch head, names saves already recorded and objects the repo holds, and marks those saves' content stored. A commit the repo already has changes nothing. The `X-Machine-Id` header names the pushing machine, as for saves.

post.summary: Ask which objects to upload
post.description: Ask which objects to upload. `missing` is the given hashes the repo holds no object for, in the order asked and without repeats. An object another repo holds is claimed instead — linked into this repo with no upload, and listed in `claimed` — when that repo's project is one the caller is a member of; held only by a project the caller is not in, it stays missing.

post.summary: Upload a pack of objects into the repo
post.description: Upload a pack of objects into the repo. The body is a run of records, `[id 32][kind u8][length u32 LE][zstd frame]`. The frame is the object's file in dit's store: it decompresses to the kind byte and the body, and id is the SHA-256 of those bytes. Records are verified as they arrive and taken into the repo in groups, and a record that fails ends the pack with the records before it kept: a frame or body over 64 MiB is a 413, an unknown kind, a frame that is not exactly one zstd frame, a frame whose first byte is not the header's kind, a hash that does not match or a body that ends inside a record a 400, and a storage cap the 413 `storage_limit`. The body must declare its `Content-Length` (a 411 without one), and a pack over the instance's upload limit is refused before a byte is read with a 413 `pack_too_large`.

post.summary: Fetch held objects as pack records
post.description: Fetch held objects as pack records. The records are in the layout the upload reads: `[id 32][kind u8][length u32 LE][zstd frame]`, one record per hash, in the order asked and without repeats. When the repo does not hold every hash, nothing is streamed: the answer is a 409 with code `objects_missing` and every missing hash, in the order asked, in `details.hashes`. A viewer of the repo's project may fetch; a stranger gets a 404.

get.summary: List your machines
get.description: List your machines. Most recently seen first, each with whether it is online (a beat within 90 s), the session it has open, the repos it tracks, the repos it has pushed to (of projects you are a member of) and its "Never here" folders. `notABounce` holds the files you marked as not a bounce, which every machine of yours shares.

get.summary: The render rejections you have made
get.description: The render rejections you have made: files that are not a bounce, which hold on every machine of yours, and the folders each machine is never to look for renders in.

post.summary: Record render rejections
post.description: Record render rejections. Answers the stored rows of those named. One already recorded is kept as it was, so a write is safe to repeat; at most 1000 per write. A folder of another account's machine is a 403 and of an unknown or removed machine a 404, and refuses the whole write.

delete.description: Delete one of your rejections. It is a "Not a bounce" file or a "Never here" folder; another account's, like none, is a 404.

put.description: Report a machine. Sent by the app on each beat; the first beat of a new id registers the machine, and each beat notes the sign-in it came from. The open session is kept only when the caller is a member of its project. A name another of the caller's machines holds is a 409 `machine_name_taken`; a machine removed from the web is a 401, the answer a signed-out app acts on.

delete.description: Remove one of your machines. It is signed out of dit: the sign-in of its last beat is revoked, so its next request is a 401. Its saves, commits and segments stay under its last name, and its name is free to reuse.
